notes: per-file times exclude the one-time grammar compile (an untimed warm-up extraction precedes timing)
range_agreement not measured: the L1 oracle reported no end line for any matched definition, so L1 can be met at most at good, never excellent (design §1.2)

sym_recall/sym_precision collapse on both subjects for a dialect-variance reason, not a query gap: isolating chinook-database's Sqlite-flavoured file alone (the same 11 tables, ANSI/SQLite DDL only) measures sym_recall 1.0, sym_precision 1.0, L1 good — every required kind extracted cleanly (verified directly, not committed as its own reading). The aggregate falls because chinook-database ships the identical schema six more times in vendor SQL DerekStride/tree-sitter-sql v0.3.11 does not parse: SqlServer's [bracket]-quoted identifiers inside a CONSTRAINT ... PRIMARY KEY CLUSTERED clause desync the parser (verified: `CONSTRAINT [PK_Album] PRIMARY KEY CLUSTERED ([AlbumId])` yields an ERROR node whose recovery misfires a bogus column_definition named "PK_Album") and Oracle/Db2-specific DDL likewise ERRORs out; sqitch's t/ fixtures are the same shape one level further (deploy/revert/verify SQL across sqlite, pg, mysql, oracle, firebird, vertica, exasol engines)

a second, independent factor: universal-ctags 6.2.1 itself is not a reliable L1 oracle for MySQL's backtick-quoted DDL — isolating chinook-database's MySQL file alone, ctags emits exactly one tag for the whole file (name "`", kind "database", from `CREATE DATABASE \`Chinook\`;`) while fathom's tree-sitter parse correctly finds all 22 definitions (verified directly); every MySQL-flavoured definition in both subjects therefore scores as an unmatched fathom def (precision loss) rather than a recall miss, through no fault of the query or grammar

engine variance is disclosed as designed (LB-Q-sql's own note): 'CONSTRAINT ... FOREIGN KEY ... REFERENCES' with a named constraint desyncs the same way as PRIMARY KEY CLUSTERED (ERROR-recovers into a usable `constraint` node — see broken.sql testdata and PROVENANCE.md); bare, unnamed FOREIGN KEY (...) REFERENCES ... parses cleanly and its FK edge is captured as an L2 reference.call on the enclosing table
disposition: deferred: target L2 not reached; L1 itself measures unmet on the merged calibration subjects, both blocked on tooling outside this dialect's queries — DerekStride/tree-sitter-sql v0.3.11 does not parse T-SQL bracket-quoted CONSTRAINT ... CLUSTERED clauses or (per the same failure shape, unverified in isolation) Oracle/Db2-specific DDL, and universal-ctags 6.2.1 mistags MySQL backtick-quoted DDL almost entirely (one bogus tag for a whole file, verified directly) rather than refusing to run — so its L1 numbers are not a trustworthy floor for MySQL content either. On standard/ANSI/SQLite-flavoured SQL alone (chinook-database's Chinook_Sqlite.sql, measured in isolation, not committed as its own reading) this same dialect reaches sym_recall 1.0, sym_precision 1.0, L1 good. L2's own blocker is separate and structural: no SCIP producer or upstream tags.scm exists for SQL, so call_recall/call_precision have no tier A/C truth to measure against at any subject (design §1.4, calibration/README.md); FK references are extracted as L2 reference.call edges regardless (dialects/sql/tags.scm), just unscored. Trigger: (a) an L1 blocker — either a tree-sitter-sql fork/version with real T-SQL and Oracle/Db2 support, or re-scoping calibration_subjects/corpus.d/sql.yaml's subpath away from chinook-database's non-Postgres variants and sqitch's non-sqlite/pg engine fixtures (an Opus call: the queue named these subjects deliberately, and this reading's own evidence is the case for revisiting them); (b) an L2 blocker — a maintained SQL SCIP producer, or an upstream tags.scm this dialect could adopt as a tier-C call oracle.
